\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{আয়ু} (āyu)}{আয়ু (āyu)}]{\bn{আয়ু} (āyu) — lifespan; length of life}

\label{lesson:BN-C491-ayu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to adopt, then the Bengali for to retire.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{আয়ু}}
\textbf{\bn{আয়ু}} — \emph{āyu} — \textquotedblleft{}lifespan; length of life\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ভালো} \bn{খাবার} \bn{আর} \bn{ব্যায়ামে} \bn{আয়ু} \bn{বাড়ে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bhālo khābār ār bæyāme āyu bāṛe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Good food and exercise lengthen your life.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{আয়ু}} (\emph{āyu}) is Sanskrit \emph{āyus}, \textquotedblleft{}life, vigour, length of life\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with the final \emph{-s} dropped.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āyu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āyu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhālo khābār ār bæyāme āyu bāṛe.} — Good food and exercise lengthen your life.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to adopt, then the Bengali for to retire, then say \emph{āyu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{আয়ু} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Lifespan; length of life\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{শ্মশান} (shmôshān)}{শ্মশান (shmôshān)}]{\bn{শ্মশান} (shmôshān) — a cremation ground}

\label{lesson:BN-C491-shmoshan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to retire, then the Bengali for lifespan.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{শ্মশান}}
\textbf{\bn{শ্মশান}} — \emph{shmôshān} — \textquotedblleft{}a cremation ground\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আমরা} \bn{দাদুকে} \bn{নদীর} \bn{ধারের} \bn{শ্মশানে} \bn{নিয়ে} \bn{গেলাম।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āmrā dāduke nôdīr dhārer shmôshāne niye gelām.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We took my grandfather to the cremation ground by the river.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{শ্মশান}} (\emph{shmôshān}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{śmaśāna}, \textquotedblleft{}a place for burning the dead\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 12658); CDIAL lists a worn-down Bengali \emph{masān} beside it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shmôshān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shmôshān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āmrā dāduke nôdīr dhārer shmôshāne niye gelām.} — We took my grandfather to the cremation ground by the river.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to retire, then the Bengali for lifespan, then say \emph{shmôshān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{শ্মশান} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A cremation ground\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{শ্রাদ্ধ} (shrāddhô)}{শ্রাদ্ধ (shrāddhô)}]{\bn{শ্রাদ্ধ} (shrāddhô) — a memorial rite for the dead}

\label{lesson:BN-C491-shraddho}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for lifespan, then the Bengali for a cremation ground.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{শ্রাদ্ধ}}
\textbf{\bn{শ্রাদ্ধ}} — \emph{shrāddhô} — \textquotedblleft{}a memorial rite for the dead\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{দাদুর} \bn{শ্রাদ্ধে} \bn{আত্মীয়রা} \bn{গ্রামে} \bn{এলেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dādur shrāddhe ātmīyôrā grāme elen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The relatives came to the village for my grandfather's memorial rite.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{শ্রাদ্ধ}} (\emph{shrāddhô}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{śrāddha}, from \emph{śraddhā}, \textquotedblleft{}faith\textquotedblright{}: a ceremony offered in faith for dead relatives (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shrāddhô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shrāddhô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dādur shrāddhe ātmīyôrā grāme elen.} — The relatives came to the village for my grandfather's memorial rite.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for lifespan, then the Bengali for a cremation ground, then say \emph{shrāddhô} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{শ্রাদ্ধ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A memorial rite for the dead\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সমবেদনা} (sômôbedônā)}{সমবেদনা (sômôbedônā)}]{\bn{সমবেদনা} (sômôbedônā) — sympathy; condolences}

\label{lesson:BN-C491-somobedona}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a cremation ground, then the Bengali for a memorial rite.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সমবেদনা}}
\textbf{\bn{সমবেদনা}} — \emph{sômôbedônā} — \textquotedblleft{}sympathy; condolences\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{প্রতিবেশীরা} \bn{এসে} \bn{আমাদের} \bn{সমবেদনা} \bn{জানাল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{prôtibeshīrā ese āmāder sômôbedônā jānālô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The neighbours came to offer us their condolences.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সমবেদনা}} (\emph{sômôbedônā}) puts Sanskrit \emph{sama}, \textquotedblleft{}same\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with \emph{vedanā}, \textquotedblleft{}feeling, pain\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 12106): feeling the same pain as someone else.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sômôbedônā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sômôbedônā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prôtibeshīrā ese āmāder sômôbedônā jānālô.} — The neighbours came to offer us their condolences.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a cremation ground, then the Bengali for a memorial rite, then say \emph{sômôbedônā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{সমবেদনা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Sympathy; condolences\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{কবর} \bn{দেওয়া} (kôbôr deoyā)}{কবর দেওয়া (kôbôr deoyā)}]{\bn{কবর} \bn{দেওয়া} (kôbôr deoyā) — to bury}

\label{lesson:BN-C491-kobor-deoya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a memorial rite, then the Bengali for condolences.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{কবর} \bn{দেওয়া}}
\textbf{\bn{কবর} \bn{দেওয়া}} — \emph{kôbôr deoyā} — \textquotedblleft{}to bury\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ছেলেরা} \bn{কুকুরটাকে} \bn{বাগানে} \bn{কবর} \bn{দিল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{chhelerā kukurṭāke bāgāne kôbôr dilô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The boys buried the dog in the garden.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{পাখিটাকে} \bn{বাগানে} \bn{কবর} \bn{দিলেন}, \emph{tini pākhiṭāke bāgāne kôbôr dilen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{কবর} \bn{দেওয়া}} (\emph{kôbôr deoyā}) is \emph{kôbôr}, \textquotedblleft{}a grave\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Arabic \emph{qabr} through Persian, the \bn{কবর} of \bn{কবরস্থান} (taught), a graveyard, with \emph{deoyā}, \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 6141).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kôbôr deoyā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kôbôr deoyā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chhelerā kukurṭāke bāgāne kôbôr dilô.} — The boys buried the dog in the garden.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a memorial rite, then the Bengali for condolences, then say \emph{kôbôr deoyā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from A New Baby to The End of a Life}

\label{lesson:BN-R491-review-485-491}



\begin{quote}
Say the Bengali for pregnant and childbirth.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item pregnant, childbirth, to be born, a baby, a cradle
  \item upbringing, to spoil (a child), to suck, to put to sleep, to crawl
  \item a relationship, a lap, to touch, to guard protectively, to stroke
  \item childhood, adolescence, youth, old age, to grow up
  \item an engagement, a household, to coax someone out of a sulk, a blessing, to touch an elder's feet
  \item a separation, a widow, an orphan, to adopt, to retire
  \item lifespan, a cremation ground, a memorial rite, condolences, to bury
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Pregnant? (\textbf{\bn{গর্ভবতী}}, \emph{gôrbhôbôtī}.) Childbirth? (\textbf{\bn{প্রসব}}, \emph{prôsôb}.) To be born? (\textbf{\bn{জন্মানো}}, \emph{jônmāno}.) A baby? (\textbf{\bn{বাচ্চা}}, \emph{bāchchā}.) A cradle? (\textbf{\bn{দোলনা}}, \emph{dolnā}.) Upbringing? (\textbf{\bn{লালনপালন}}, \emph{lālônpālôn}.) To spoil (a child)? (\textbf{\bn{প্রশ্রয়} \bn{দেওয়া}}, \emph{prôshrôy deoyā}.) To suck? (\textbf{\bn{চোষা}}, \emph{choshā}.) To put to sleep? (\textbf{\bn{ঘুম} \bn{পাড়ানো}}, \emph{ghum pāṛāno}.) To crawl? (\textbf{\bn{হামাগুড়ি} \bn{দেওয়া}}, \emph{hāmāguṛi deoyā}.) A relationship? (\textbf{\bn{সম্পর্ক}}, \emph{sômpôrkô}.) A lap? (\textbf{\bn{কোল}}, \emph{kol}.) To touch? (\textbf{\bn{ছোঁয়া}}, \emph{chhõyā}.) To guard protectively? (\textbf{\bn{আগলানো}}, \emph{āglāno}.) To stroke? (\textbf{\bn{বোলানো}}, \emph{bolāno}.) Childhood? (\textbf{\bn{শৈশব}}, \emph{shoishôb}.) Adolescence? (\textbf{\bn{কৈশোর}}, \emph{koishor}.) Youth? (\textbf{\bn{যৌবন}}, \emph{joubôn}.) Old age? (\textbf{\bn{বার্ধক্য}}, \emph{bārdhôkyô}.) To grow up? (\textbf{\bn{বেড়ে} \bn{ওঠা}}, \emph{beṛe oṭhā}.) An engagement? (\textbf{\bn{বাগদান}}, \emph{bāgdān}.) A household? (\textbf{\bn{সংসার}}, \emph{sôngsār}.) To coax someone out of a sulk? (\textbf{\bn{মান} \bn{ভাঙানো}}, \emph{mān bhāngāno}.) A blessing? (\textbf{\bn{আশীর্বাদ}}, \emph{āshīrbād}.) To touch an elder's feet? (\textbf{\bn{প্রণাম} \bn{করা}}, \emph{prônām kôrā}.) A separation? (\textbf{\bn{বিচ্ছেদ}}, \emph{bichchhed}.) A widow? (\textbf{\bn{বিধবা}}, \emph{bidhôbā}.) An orphan? (\textbf{\bn{অনাথ}}, \emph{ônāth}.) To adopt? (\textbf{\bn{দত্তক} \bn{নেওয়া}}, \emph{dôttôk neoyā}.) To retire? (\textbf{\bn{অবসর} \bn{নেওয়া}}, \emph{ôbôsôr neoyā}.) Lifespan? (\textbf{\bn{আয়ু}}, \emph{āyu}.) A cremation ground? (\textbf{\bn{শ্মশান}}, \emph{shmôshān}.) A memorial rite? (\textbf{\bn{শ্রাদ্ধ}}, \emph{shrāddhô}.) Condolences? (\textbf{\bn{সমবেদনা}}, \emph{sômôbedônā}.) To bury? (\textbf{\bn{কবর} \bn{দেওয়া}}, \emph{kôbôr deoyā}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
